title: Which cards give the largest sum and the smallest difference?
description: Two sets of cards numbered one to nine fill a row of seven boxes and a row of five boxes. The highest places get the biggest digits for the largest sum, and the top number is made small and the bottom number big for the smallest difference.
teaching_notes: One idea: rank the places by value, then deal out the digits. Watch for students who forget that each digit has only two cards, and who put big digits in the top number when the difference must be small.

source: Figure it Out, Q9 (two sets of cards)
video_script.why: The child knows that a digit in a higher place is worth more, and now uses that to place cards for the largest sum and the smallest difference.
video_script.substitution: Rank the places by value; for the sum, give the highest places the biggest digits; for the difference, make the top number small and the bottom number big.
video_script.anchor: two rows of empty boxes, seven above and five below, lined up on the right, with two sets of cards numbered one to nine
video_script.payoff_line: Rank the places by value, then deal the digits out

final_answer.spoken: the largest sum is one crore seventy five thousand three hundred eight

maths_rules: two sets of cards 1 to 9 give each digit twice, 18 cards in all; 14 boxes are filled
largest sum: the two highest places (top only) get 9 and 9; each lower place has a box in both numbers and takes a repeated digit: 8 8, 7 7, 6 6, 5 5, 4 4; top 99,87,654, bottom 87,654
smallest difference: top as small as possible, bottom as large as possible; top 11,22,334 (1 1 2 2 3 3 4), bottom 99,887 (9 9 8 8 7); no digit is used more than twice
video_script.design: One idea: rank the places by value, then deal the digits out. The two rows of boxes stay in the anchor band; the working band shows the two fillings. The two questions are named by their idea, not by letters. No hard clear.
open_questions: The book answer key gives 1,00,54,320 for the largest sum; the worklist and a direct calculation give 1,00,75,308, which the video follows.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, for the smallest difference, make the top number small and the bottom number big.

<bookmark mark='m4'/>The bottom number takes nine, nine, eight, eight and seven.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>The top number is eleven lakh twenty two thousand three hundred thirty four.
The bottom number is ninety nine thousand eight hundred eighty seven.
<bookmark mark='m6'/>Their difference is ten lakh twenty two thousand four hundred forty seven.
